svg.text: 23 drugs are short in three countries at once
Every substance appearing on the United States, French and Australian shortage registers simultaneously, with the name each
of 573 distinct ingredients across all three
23 substances on all three registers, from one capture of each taken 2026-09-10. Four cytotoxics, five anaesthesia and seizure drugs, and otherwise the cheapest drugs in the formulary.
The join is an RxNorm ingredient code, not a name — so salt forms collapse and the French 'rifampicine' meets the American 'Rifampin'. The names are printed so it can be checked.
A name-stem join gets this wrong in both directions — see 2-string-vs-code. It misses mesalamine and rifampin, and it merges three different insulins into one.
Register totals are NOT comparable — FDA records per package NDC, ANSM and TGA per product. Only the overlap is.
One capture each, taken 2026-09-10, so this is a cross-section and cannot say whether the overlap is growing.
